house_rules: Nothing on trlibrary.com changes without the communications team's approval. Once approved, make the change (if you have Drupal access) or hand it over ready to paste; never stop at a recommendation when a work-queue task can be carried out.
After any change, log it in config/changes.yml (date, page, kind, what) so the next run holds the page and reports before/after numbers.
Pages listed under 'Recently changed' were just edited: don't recommend changing them again until their hold ends; judge them by the before/after numbers.
Never invent historical facts, dates, names, prices or hours. Use only what the page already says, or flag it for verification.
Never quote or paraphrase Theodore Roosevelt. Say 'consider a verified TR quote about X' instead.
Voice: friendly, plain, concrete (a knowledgeable park ranger, not a professor). Keep 'we/our/us' to a minimum.
No specific years in visitor copy; write seasons as months.
A Library visit takes about 3 1/2 hours. Never present a shorter visit as typical.
Nonpartisan: no current political figures or debates.
Page titles: the site appends ' | Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library' automatically; suggest only the page-specific part, 60 characters or fewer.
Meta descriptions: 120-155 characters with a reason to click.
Recommend selectively: lead with one to three moves (start from 'This week's moves'), then a short 'what else we checked' list, each with a one-line reason it can wait.

Size gains honestly: name how the gain happens (a new ranking, a higher position, or more clicks at the same position); a page that already ranks already gets some clicks; upside figures rank options and are never forecasts.
Website changes are made in Drupal Layout Builder by the TRPL team; bugs and features go to the developers (FiveJars).

content_additions.draft:
Quick Facts: The Brownsville Affair
- What happened: On August 13–14, 1906, shots in Brownsville, Texas killed a bartender and wounded a police officer. Townspeople blamed soldiers from the all-Black 25th Infantry Regiment stationed at Fort Brown.
- Roosevelt's action: In November 1906, President Roosevelt discharged 167 soldiers without honor, individual hearings, or court-martial.
- The outcome: In 1972, the U.S. Army overturned the ruling and granted honorable discharges. In 1973, Dorsie Willis, the only surviving member, received a compensation payment.

content_additions.suggestion: Weave common historical alternate names ('Brownsville incident', 'Brownsville raid', 'Brownsville affray') into the opening section to help searchers find the event under varied terms.
content_additions.draft: Sometimes referred to as the Brownsville incident, raid, or affray, the episode began on the night of August 13–14, 1906, when gunfire broke out near Fort Brown.

content_additions.draft: Quick Definition: Announced in an Annual Message to Congress in December 1904, the Roosevelt Corollary expanded the Monroe Doctrine. Where the original doctrine warned European powers to keep out of the Western Hemisphere, Roosevelt asserted that the United States would act as an 'international police power'—stepping in directly if Latin American nations faced chronic instability or unpaid foreign debts.

content_additions.suggestion: Add a side-by-side comparison box or subheading that explicitly contrasts the two policies, directly satisfying comparison queries.
content_additions.draft:
Monroe Doctrine vs. Roosevelt Corollary:
- Monroe Doctrine (1823): A defensive warning telling European empires to keep their hands off the Western Hemisphere.
- Roosevelt Corollary (1904): An active policy claiming the United States had the authority to step into Latin American affairs to police debts and maintain order before European nations intervened.

content_additions.draft:
### Who Were the Rough Riders?
The Rough Riders were the 1st U.S. Volunteer Cavalry, an extraordinary regiment of more than 1,000 men organized to fight in Cuba during the Spanish-American War. Commanded by Colonel Leonard Wood and Theodore Roosevelt, the unit brought together Southwestern cowboys, Ivy League athletes, Native American scouts, lawmen, and miners into a single force.

content_additions.for_query: why were the rough riders important
content_additions.suggestion: Add a dedicated subhead and brief section near the conclusion addressing the historical significance of the regiment, which is a common search question.
content_additions.draft:
### Why Were the Rough Riders Important?
The regiment proved that volunteers from completely different walks of life could pull together into an effective fighting force. Their charges at Las Guasimas and Kettle Hill helped break Spanish defensive lines around Santiago. Back home, accounts of their battlefield courage captured public attention and turned Theodore Roosevelt into a celebrated national figure, lifting him to the governorship of New York within months.

What Roosevelt Did That Had Never Been Done Before
Before Roosevelt, no president had ever created a federal bird reservation, proclaimed a national monument, or summoned every state governor to the White House to focus on natural resources. In total, he placed roughly 230 million acres under public protection — doubling the national park system and establishing the U.S. Forest Service.

content_additions.draft:
### What Was Theodore Roosevelt's Workout Routine?
Roosevelt treated physical conditioning as a daily obligation. His regular routine brought together several demanding disciplines:
- Heavy bag work and sparring in the boxing ring
- Calisthenics, running, and weightlifting
- Point-to-point cross-country hikes, scrambling over rocks and through streams
- Daily horseback riding on rugged trails
- Open-water swimming and rowing in all seasons
- Jiu-jitsu and wrestling sessions to sharpen balance and leverage

content_additions.suggestion: Add a quick-reference callout in the boxing section highlighting key facts about his boxing career, including his training at Harvard, White House sparring, and the bout that impaired his vision.
content_additions.draft:
### Fast Facts: Roosevelt in the Ring
- Started boxing as a teenager under former prize-fighter John Long after an encounter on a stagecoach ride to Moosehead Lake.
- Continued competitive sparring as an undergraduate at Harvard.
- Kept up regular sparring sessions with military aides inside the White House during his presidency.
- Stepped away from the ring after a punch from a young artillery captain injured his left eye and left the vision permanently dimmed.

sitewide_issues.title: Sitewide markup doesn't link to the Library's Wikipedia entry
sitewide_issues.detail: sameAs lists only social accounts. Wikipedia and Wikidata links are how search engines and AI tools confirm that trlibrary.com is the same Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library they know about.
sitewide_issues.fix: Add these to sameAs in the sitewide schema.

sitewide_issues.title: Restaurant and store hours are listed as the museum's hours
sitewide_issues.detail: The museum entity carries 15 hours entries, including restaurant, store hours. Machines can't tell which hours mean the museum is open.
sitewide_issues.fix: Keep only museum hours on the Library entity. Give the restaurant and the store their own entities (Restaurant, Store) with their hours, linked with containsPlace.

sitewide_issues.title: No admission information in the markup
sitewide_issues.detail: “How much are tickets?” is one of the most common visitor questions. The markup has no price or ticket link.
sitewide_issues.fix: Add admission offers (and isAccessibleForFree: false) to the Library entity.

sitewide_issues.title: 35 unaliased /node/ URLs are in the sitemap
sitewide_issues.detail: These are duplicate addresses for pages that have proper URLs (or old, unpublished-looking items). They waste crawler time and split signals between two addresses.
sitewide_issues.fix: Ask FiveJars to leave unaliased /node/ URLs out of the XML sitemap.

sitewide_issues.title: The Theodore Roosevelt entity has 2 values to fix
sitewide_issues.detail: Every /tr page repeats this entity, so a wrong or missing value repeats on all of them. alternateName lacks “Teddy Roosevelt” · award holds several honors in one string; list each one separately
sitewide_issues.fix: Edit the meta tags of the “Who was TR” hub page (Schema.org Person). The values are set once there and FiveJars' code prints them on every /tr page. Check names and dates against the Historical Accuracy Standard before saving.

sitewide_issues.title: 273 pages have dates without a colon in the time zone
sitewide_issues.detail: For example datePublished “2020-10-27T06:00:00-0600” on /about/press/press-releases/trplf-announces-100-million-commitments-unlocks-50-million-state. Strict ISO 8601 wants “-06:00”, and some validators reject the short form.
sitewide_issues.fix: In the Drupal schema templates, format dateModified, datePublished, endDate, startDate with the PHP date format “c” (e.g. 2020-10-27T06:00:00-06:00).

sitewide_issues.title: The live llms.txt has drifted from the site: 19 pages to add
sitewide_issues.detail: www.trlibrary.com/llms.txt lists 200 pages; this week's draft from the sitemap lists 216. Sections added by hand in Drupal are left alone.
sitewide_issues.fix: Edit the sections at /admin/content/llms-txt/sections: add the new pages under their heading and remove or repoint the links that left the sitemap. The draft has the wording for each new line.

sitewide_issues.title: 251 articles use the site logo as their Article image
sitewide_issues.detail: The page has its own share image (og:image), but the Article markup points to the generic logo, so search and AI previews show the logo instead of the page's picture.
sitewide_issues.fix: Map the Article image to the page's share image (og:image), falling back to the logo only when a page has none.

sitewide_issues.title: 91 articles are labelled og:type “website”
sitewide_issues.detail: Social and AI previews treat them as generic pages rather than articles.
sitewide_issues.fix: Set og:type to “article” on /tr, press release and podcast templates (Drupal Metatag).

mainEntity.name: HOW CAN I DONATE?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can make a secure online payment through the website: trlibrary.com/donate . Or, send a check payable to the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library Foundation to: TR Library 401 E Main Ave Ste 201 Bismarck, ND 58501.

mainEntity.name: IF I JOIN A BENEFACTOR SOCIETY, HOW WILL MY DONATION BE USED?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your donation will provide funding for physical and virtual programing and operations to explore the life, legacy, and enduring relevance of Theodore Roosevelt.

mainEntity.name: MAY I DIRECT MY GIFT TO SUPPORT A SPECIFIC AREA OF TRPL?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most powerful way to support the Library is with an unrestricted gift. Unrestricted support gives us the flexibility to direct resources where the need and opportunity are greatest — such as to the programs, conservation, and educational work that will define the Library's future — and it ensures your generosity has the broadest possible impact. That said, we're always glad to hear from benefactors with a particular passion. If you'd like to support a specific area, we welcome the conversation and would be pleased to explore opportunities that align with your interests and the Library's long-term vision. However you choose to give, your support will be recognized through the appropriate Benefactor Society.

mainEntity.name: WHAT IS THE TAX-EXEMPT STATUS OF THE THEODORE ROOSEVELT PRESIDENTIAL LIBRARY?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library Foundation manages the Library and fundraises on its behalf. The Foundation is a tax-exempt 501(c)(3) organization.

mainEntity.name: WILL MY GIFT BE TAX DEDUCTIBLE?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, gifts are 100% tax-deductible to the full extent of the law.

mainEntity.name: WILL I RECEIVE A TAX RECEIPT?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, a tax receipt will be provided.

mainEntity.name: WHAT ARE SOME OF THE BENEFACTOR SOCIETY BENEFITS?

acceptedAnswer.text: Benefits include a special welcome packet, the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library e-newsletter and digital recognition (unless anonymity is requested). Additional opportunities for recognition are available based on level of support.

mainEntity.name: HOW LONG DOES MY BENEFACTOR SOCIETY PARTICIPATION LAST?

acceptedAnswer.text: Benefactor Society participation recognizes the total impact of your cumulative giving.

mainEntity.name: DO YOU SELL OR SHARE BENEFACTOR INFORMATION WITH THIRD PARTIES?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, we do not.

mainEntity.name: MAY I MAKE AN ANONYMOUS GIFT TO JOIN A BENEFACTOR SOCIETY?

acceptedAnswer.text: Certainly, simply specify your desire to remain anonymous when you make your gift and your request will be honored.

mainEntity.name: WILL MY NAME BE PRINTED IN MATERIALS OR PUBLISHED IN ANY WAY?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, digital recognition (unless anonymity is requested) and additional opportunities for recognition are available based on level of support.

mainEntity.name: I HAVE MORE QUESTIONS. WHO CAN I REACH OUT TO?

acceptedAnswer.text: Please contact us at giving@trlibrary.com .

workflow: Pick tasks from the top of the queue (or a page job, to do everything on one page at once). Pages marked held changed recently and are being measured: leave their titles, descriptions and copy alone (adding markup or links to them is fine).
Write the exact change: new title/description, the sentence with the link, the markup fields, the redirect. Use only facts already on the page.
Get approval from the communications team before changing the live site. Merges, archiving and anything sitewide always need approval.
If you have Drupal admin access, make TRPL-owned changes yourself using the recipe. Content changes to a page can be saved as a draft first.
For FiveJars-owned tasks, write a Basecamp to-do: what's wrong, example URLs, the ready-to-paste JSON-LD or setting, how to check.
Check the live page afterwards (view source for meta tags and JSON-LD; follow redirects with curl).
Log each change in config/changes.yml (date, page, kind, what) so the next run holds the page and reports before/after numbers.

recipes.meta: Edit the node (/node/NID/edit) > 'Customize meta tags'. Basic tags: Page title '<title> | [site:name]' (page part 60 characters or fewer) and Description (120-155 characters). Set Open Graph og:title/og:description and Twitter card title/description to match. Save with 'Save' (keeps the moderation state). If the save seems to do nothing, look for a validation error further down the form.
recipes.h1_missing: Open the page's Layout (/node/NID/layout). Make sure the top section shows the page title block (Content fields > Title), which renders as the H1; or change the first heading in the top text block to Heading 1. Save layout.
recipes.h1_multiple: Open the Layout. Keep one H1 (normally the page title block). In any text block whose heading is set to Heading 1, change it to Heading 2. Save layout.
recipes.chain: Configuration > Search and metadata > URL redirects: find the redirects for this address and point the first one straight at the final page. Update any links on the site that use the old address.
recipes.canonical: Edit the node > 'Customize meta tags' > Advanced > Canonical URL: clear it (Drupal then uses the page's own address) or set it to the live page it should point to.
recipes.headings: Open the Layout. In the text blocks, change the heading levels so they step down one at a time (H2 under the page title, H3 under an H2). Headings used just for size should be styled text instead.
recipes.deep: Link to the page from its section's hub page or a related, well-visited page, so people (and crawlers) reach it in three or four clicks.
recipes.alias: Edit the node > URL alias: give it a readable path that fits its section; save. The /node/NID address keeps working and the sitemap will list the readable one. (The lasting fix is FiveJars keeping unaliased /node/ URLs out of the XML sitemap.)
recipes.sitemap: This sitemap URL redirects to another page. Edit the old node > XML sitemap > Inclusion: Excluded, or archive the node if it's retired (a 301 stays in place).
recipes.thin: Only for pages people find in Google. Add useful, verified copy from the page's own subject (what it is, why it matters, what to do next, links to related pages). Never invent facts; draft for review.
recipes.link: Open the source page's Layout. Edit the text block that contains the context sentence and turn the [[bracketed]] words into a link to the target path (relative, e.g. /tr/tr-shot). Don't write new sentences just to hold a link. Save the block, then Save layout.
recipes.orphan: Add 2-3 links to this page from the pages listed under 'link from' (each has the sentence and words to link).
recipes.related: These two pages cover the same subject without linking to each other. Add one natural link each way, in the paragraph where the shared subject comes up.
recipes.duplicate_topic: Two pages compete for one subject. Pick the stronger page (clicks, depth), move anything unique onto it, then archive the other and add a 301 from its alias and /node/NID. Get approval first; draft before publishing.
recipes.redirect: Configuration > Search and metadata > URL redirects > Add redirect: From = broken path, To = target, 301. If Drupal warns the path looks valid, submit again. Bulk: import redirects.csv. Also fix the link on the source page when the target is known.
recipes.via_redirect: Edit the link on each source page so it points straight at the final address.
recipes.schema_article: Edit the node > 'Customize meta tags' > Schema.org Article: @type Article; headline = the page title; description = the meta description; about = Theodore Roosevelt; author and publisher = the Library; dateModified = [node:changed:html_datetime]. Don't paste raw JSON-LD into a text block (it's stripped).
recipes.schema_person: Edit the node > 'Customize meta tags' > Schema.org Person: name, description, image, and sameAs (Wikipedia/Wikidata only when verified).
recipes.schema_event: Edit the node > 'Customize meta tags' > Schema.org Event: name, startDate/endDate (ISO 8601 with a colon in the offset, e.g. 2026-12-04T18:00:00-06:00), location = the Library, offers (price, ticket URL) only from the page.
recipes.striking: Open the page and make it the best answer to that exact search: use the search's words in the title or a heading, answer it plainly in the first paragraph, add the specifics people want (facts already on the site), and link to it from 2-3 related pages. Don't rewrite a page that already ranks in the top 3 for its main search.
recipes.outreach: Read the page. If it's a list of things to do or a travel guide that names nearby attractions, find the author or the update/contact link and ask to be added, with a two-sentence blurb (what the Library is, why it's worth the stop, about 3 1/2 hours) and a photo. Draft the note for approval; nothing goes out without it.
recipes.fanout: These are the searches the assistants ran before answering a question where they left the Library out. Find the trlibrary.com page that should answer each one (or note that none does). Strengthen that page for the search: say it in the title or a heading and answer it in the first paragraph, with facts already on the site. If no page fits, propose one.
recipes.global: Sitewide (Global) meta tags: change them only through Configuration > Development > Configuration synchronization > Import > Single item (Simple configuration, metatag.metatag_defaults.global), then clear all caches. Never save the Global defaults form itself: it drops fields.
recipes.fivejars: Write it up as a Basecamp to-do for FiveJars: what's wrong, example URLs, the ready-to-paste JSON-LD or setting, and how to check it.

tasks.title: Restaurant and store hours are listed as the museum's hours
tasks.how: Keep only museum hours on the Library entity. Give the restaurant and the store their own entities (Restaurant, Store) with their hours, linked with containsPlace. Write it up as a Basecamp to-do for FiveJars: what's wrong, example URLs, the ready-to-paste JSON-LD or setting, and how to check it. The hours come from the dynamic opening-hours plugin (schema_organization_opening_hours_specification_dynamic = 1), which reads every row of TRPL > Operating Hours. Ask FiveJars to emit only the museum rows on the Library entity and put the restaurant and store rows on their own Restaurant and Store entities via containsPlace.
tasks.detail: The museum entity carries 15 hours entries, including restaurant, store hours. Machines can't tell which hours mean the museum is open.
tasks.done_when: The issue no longer appears in schema.json after the next weekly run

mainEntity.name: HOW CAN I DONATE?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can make a secure online payment through the website: trlibrary.com/donate . Or, send a check payable to the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library Foundation to: TR Library 401 E Main Ave Ste 201 Bismarck, ND 58501.

mainEntity.name: IF I JOIN A BENEFACTOR SOCIETY, HOW WILL MY DONATION BE USED?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your donation will provide funding for physical and virtual programing and operations to explore the life, legacy, and enduring relevance of Theodore Roosevelt.

mainEntity.name: MAY I DIRECT MY GIFT TO SUPPORT A SPECIFIC AREA OF TRPL?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most powerful way to support the Library is with an unrestricted gift. Unrestricted support gives us the flexibility to direct resources where the need and opportunity are greatest — such as to the programs, conservation, and educational work that will define the Library's future — and it ensures your generosity has the broadest possible impact. That said, we're always glad to hear from benefactors with a particular passion. If you'd like to support a specific area, we welcome the conversation and would be pleased to explore opportunities that align with your interests and the Library's long-term vision. However you choose to give, your support will be recognized through the appropriate Benefactor Society.

mainEntity.name: WHAT IS THE TAX-EXEMPT STATUS OF THE THEODORE ROOSEVELT PRESIDENTIAL LIBRARY?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library Foundation manages the Library and fundraises on its behalf. The Foundation is a tax-exempt 501(c)(3) organization.

mainEntity.name: WILL MY GIFT BE TAX DEDUCTIBLE?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, gifts are 100% tax-deductible to the full extent of the law.

mainEntity.name: WILL I RECEIVE A TAX RECEIPT?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, a tax receipt will be provided.

mainEntity.name: WHAT ARE SOME OF THE BENEFACTOR SOCIETY BENEFITS?

acceptedAnswer.text: Benefits include a special welcome packet, the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library e-newsletter and digital recognition (unless anonymity is requested). Additional opportunities for recognition are available based on level of support.

mainEntity.name: HOW LONG DOES MY BENEFACTOR SOCIETY PARTICIPATION LAST?

acceptedAnswer.text: Benefactor Society participation recognizes the total impact of your cumulative giving.

mainEntity.name: DO YOU SELL OR SHARE BENEFACTOR INFORMATION WITH THIRD PARTIES?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, we do not.

mainEntity.name: MAY I MAKE AN ANONYMOUS GIFT TO JOIN A BENEFACTOR SOCIETY?

acceptedAnswer.text: Certainly, simply specify your desire to remain anonymous when you make your gift and your request will be honored.

mainEntity.name: WILL MY NAME BE PRINTED IN MATERIALS OR PUBLISHED IN ANY WAY?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, digital recognition (unless anonymity is requested) and additional opportunities for recognition are available based on level of support.

mainEntity.name: I HAVE MORE QUESTIONS. WHO CAN I REACH OUT TO?

acceptedAnswer.text: Please contact us at giving@trlibrary.com .
